product.summary: Ember & Ash, a fictional specialist shop for studio ceramics: a catalogue of a few hundred pieces by named makers, each in small runs with glaze variants and real stock limits.

audience.who: home cooks and collectors buying one or two pieces
audience.environment: evening browsing, comparing glazes, buying on impulse

audience.who: restaurants and gift buyers ordering sets
audience.environment: filtering by maker, size and availability, ordering several

requirements.text: The pieces are the interface: photographs large and true to colour, chrome minimal and warm.
Filtering by maker, form, glaze and availability is the main navigation and must work with a thumb and with a keyboard.
Stock is real and small: availability (in stock, last few, sold out, made to order) is visible on every card and detail, never by colour alone.
Variants (glaze, size) change the photograph, the price and the stock; the choice is never ambiguous.
Adding to the bag confirms without leaving the page; the bag is reachable from anywhere and keyboard-operable.
Brand: clay, ash glaze and ember; warm neutrals, a terracotta accent, serif headings for maker names, a sans for everything operational.
Cards align on a strict grid so glazes can be compared across rows; prices in tabular figures.
Motion is limited to feedback (bag count, variant change) and image loading; nothing animates while the user compares.
A dark theme exists for evening browsing, with photographs untouched.

direction.statement:
Warm and exact. Photographs carry the page; the interface is a quiet frame of clay-toned neutrals with one ember accent for actions.
Maker names in a serif, everything the shopper operates in a plain sans with tabular prices.
A strict card grid so glazes read across rows like a shelf.
references: a potter's shelf: pieces in rows, labels small and consistent
a museum shop catalogue: one photograph per object, generous margins
a market stall price card: the number first

decisions.choice: Fraunces Variable for maker names and section titles at a 1.2 ratio; Inter Variable for product names, prices, filters and buttons; prices in tabular figures at 16px minimum.

Warm neutrals tinted from clay (#9a7b63) on a warm off-white canvas; terracotta accent (#b4502e) only on add-to-bag, the bag badge and active filters; availability uses words plus a small shape, colour is secondary.
4px base; 16px card padding, 24px grid gutter, 48px between catalogue sections; filters as 36px chips.
Comfortable: cards with the photograph at 4:5, name, maker, price and availability in four short lines.

Catalogue: filter rail on the left at 1024px and above, a filter sheet on smaller screens; a 2/3/4-column card grid by width; product detail with the gallery on the left two thirds and a sticky purchase panel.
Soft: 6px on cards and controls, 9999 on chips and the bag badge.
Flat cards with a 1px border; one shadow level for the bag drawer and menus; photographs never get shadows.
160ms for chips and buttons, 240ms for the bag drawer, a 320ms crossfade when a variant changes the photograph; the bag badge bumps once; reduced motion cuts.
Studio photographs on a neutral surface, fixed 4:5 boxes with a placeholder of the piece's dominant colour so the grid never shifts; alt text names the piece, the maker and the glaze.

Hover lifts nothing: cards gain a stronger border; the chosen variant has a 2px accent ring; sold-out cards keep full contrast with a 'Sold out' label; focus is a 2px ring in the foreground colour with 2px offset.
Dark theme with clay-dark surfaces; photographs keep their white studio surface so colours stay true.
Filters are checkboxes and radios inside fieldsets with legends; variant swatches are radio buttons with visible labels; the bag is a dialog with focus trap and restore; targets 44px on the phone.
Breakpoints 640, 768, 1024, 1280 by card count; the purchase panel becomes a sticky bottom bar under 768px with price and add-to-bag.

states.hover: stronger border on cards, one step darker on actions

imagery.policy: studio photographs on a neutral surface in fixed 4:5 boxes with dominant-colour placeholders; alt names piece, maker and glaze
